title: ClientMessage
description: Discriminated union of all client (phone) -> server (Pi) messages. See design doc §7.1.

t0.description: Phone clock at send, in milliseconds.

StartMapping.description: Begin a capture. The CLIENT is the configuration authority: it measured the scene (light level, camera frame rate), so it chooses the code carrier and signaling rate. Omitted fields fall back to server defaults — the server needs no command-line configuration.

symbols.description: Data-symbol alphabet size (see code_params.json). Chosen by the client from measured chroma SNR: good conditions -> 4 (2 bits/frame, ~half the data frames), marginal -> 2 (max hue separation). Null/omitted -> server default (2).

bitPeriodMs.description: Signaling rate (per symbol window). Chosen by the client so each window spans >= ~3 camera frame intervals — in low light the camera lengthens exposure and drops fps, so the client requests a slower code. Null/omitted -> server default.

brightness.description: LED output brightness scale (see code_params.json). Servoed by the client against measured bloom/wash-out. Null/omitted -> server default (1.0).

Configure.description: Mid-capture renegotiation: rebuild the code-book from the active capture's parameters overlaid with the provided fields and restamp the pattern clock epoch. Detections already collected are kept — they are (ledId, pixel, pose) records, independent of the signaling that produced them. The server replies with pattern_state carrying the new epoch + codeParams; pattern followers (the wall, the M1 driver) pick the change up through their normal pattern polling. Sent when measured conditions drift during a capture (e.g. the camera drops to 15 fps in dimming light and the current bit period no longer spans 3 camera frames). Errors with no_session when no capture is active.

solveOnHost.description: Where the final solve runs (solver placement, decided by the client's init-time benchmark). True/null/omitted: the server reconstructs and replies result_ready (the classic flow). False: the server only stops the capture and persists the log, replying mapping_stopped; the client solves locally in its wasm solver and uploads the map via submit_map.

SubmitMap.description: Upload a client-solved OutputMap (the phone-side final solve, produced by the wasm solver after stop_mapping with solveOnHost=false). The server persists it to the map store exactly as if it had solved it, and replies result_ready so the download flow is identical for both placements.

ImuBatch.description: A batch of inertial samples from the capture device (~1 s cadence, ~60 Hz samples). Sent by the WebXR-free capture path so the server can jointly solve camera poses and LED positions (docs/vio-exploration.md): the gyro dead-reckons between camera frames; the accelerometer provides metric scale and gravity. Samples are in the CAMERA frame (+X right, +Y up, -Z look) — the CLIENT applies its device-specific DeviceMotion axis mapping before sending, because only it knows the device. No reply; persisted in the session log.

t.description: Phone monotonic clock at the sample, ms — same domain as DetectionRecord.tCaptureMs.

gyro.description: Angular rate [x, y, z] in rad/s, camera frame.

accel.description: Specific force (a − g) [x, y, z] in m/s², camera frame. A device at rest reads +9.81 along whichever camera axis points up.

ExposureReport.description: Periodic camera/exposure telemetry from the capture client (~every 2 s while capturing). The web client cannot read the camera's real 3A/ISP state (WebXR raw camera access exposes only the texture), so it reports software estimates: luminance statistics from an unthresholded downsampled readback plus the measured frame cadence (long exposure in low light lowers fps, making frameIntervalMs a shutter-speed proxy). iso/exposureTimeMs are reserved for clients that CAN read the 3A state (a native app, or a future web API); ambientIntensity comes from WebXR light estimation when available. The server appends reports to the session log for offline diagnosis; no reply.

tCaptureMs.description: Phone monotonic clock at the end of the measurement window, ms.

frameIntervalMs.description: Median camera frame interval over the window, ms. Rises when low light lengthens exposure — the shutter-speed proxy the signaling rate is negotiated against.

meanLuma.description: Mean scene luminance in [0,1] from the unthresholded downsampled frame.

clipFrac.description: Fraction of pixels at/above 0.98 — saturated highlights (blooming LEDs / clipped chroma).

blobCount.description: Median detector blobs per frame over the window, at the current threshold.

detectorThreshold.description: Detector luminance threshold in effect during the window.

iso.description: Real sensor ISO from the 3A/ISP, when the platform exposes it (native clients). Null/omitted on the web client.

exposureTimeMs.description: Real sensor exposure time from the 3A/ISP, ms, when the platform exposes it. Null/omitted on the web client.

ambientIntensity.description: WebXR light-estimation primary light intensity (max RGB component, relative units), when the session grants light-estimation.

GetPattern.description: Ask for the current pattern-clock state. Sent by pattern followers (e.g. the virtual LED wall test page) that render the blink code but do not own the capture session.

GetLiveMap.description: Poll the continuous solver for the latest interim reconstruction of the active capture. Polling also drives the solver: the server kicks a new solve when detections have arrived since the last one.

GetSolveStatus.description: Poll the FINAL solve's progress (after stop_mapping, while the reply is pending): optimizer progress, current reprojection rms, and the converging interim LED positions for a live preview. Reply: solve_status.

ColorBlock.description: A contiguous run of same-color LEDs in a counting pattern.

SetCountingPattern.description: LED-counting handshake (design doc §7.9): command the player to display a static color-block pattern. Blocks paint [start, start+count) in rgb; LEDs not covered by any block are off. Painting past the physical strip end is expected — that IS the probe: the phone binary-searches the strip length by observing which blocks light. Empty blocks = all off (ends the counting display). Reply: counting_state.

channel.description: Player output channel; null/omitted -> 0. The Pi has one channel; the ESP32 may drive several RMT outputs.

SetLedCount.description: Report the LED count the counting handshake detected so the player persists it as the channel's configured strip length (used to default codeParams.ledCount and to bound playback buffers). Reply: led_count_state.

SubmitTopology.description: Upload the skeletonized topology for a stored map (phone-side skeletonization, Phase F). The player persists it next to the map — it drives the O(N) pulse illuminate — and replies result_ready with the map id, mirroring submit_map.

SetPlayback.description: Playback control (design doc §7.8): select the running effect and overlay its params. 'off' stops playback and is supported by every player; other effect names are player-capability-dependent (a player replies error code='unsupported_effect' for engines it does not ship, listing what it does). Reply: playback_state with the effective configuration.

effect.description: Effect name: 'off' (universal), 'solid', 'pulse', 'rainbow', ... — an open set, validated by the player.

mapId.description: Which stored map/topology to play on; null/omitted keeps the player's current selection (or its only stored map).

GetPlayback.description: Poll the current playback state (for a config UI attaching to a running player). Reply: playback_state.

GetFrameTiming.description: Drain the player's rendered-frame timing log. The player samples its monotonic clock as it pushes each mapping-pattern frame to the LEDs; the phone polls this while tracing and forwards the samples to the trace server, so pattern-generator stutter is visible offline. Reply: frame_timing.
